description:
How people get around and get online: households with no vehicle available, as a count and a share ([B25044](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25044)); commute mode shares for driving alone, public transportation, walking or cycling, and working from home ([B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301)); the share of commutes of 45 minutes or more ([B08303](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08303)); and the shares of households with no internet access and no computing device ([B28002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B28002), [B28001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B28001)).

Curated indicators for all **3,235** counties and county equivalents in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The Bureau also publishes 1-year estimates at this geography; the 5-year release is used throughout this catalog so every geography in it is the same vintage and directly comparable.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Counties are the coarsest geography most questions are actually asked at, and the most reliable in this catalog below state level: the median coefficient of variation on `median_hh_income` is **0.042** here against 0.125 at tract level (measured). One context column breaks the catalog's own rule — `population_moe` is NULL on **3,103 of the 3,235 rows**, only 132 small rural counties carrying a margin on `population` — so read `population` here as a count to use rather than an estimate to put an interval on. `pct_commute_transit` is the column to handle with care: only 2,417 of the 3,235 counties publish a coefficient of variation for it at all, and **69.9%** of those are above 0.40 (measured). Most counties have too little transit commuting to estimate a share precisely, and that is a finding rather than a defect.

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for counties and county equivalents (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The boundary vintage matches the estimate vintage.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 13 county equivalents in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of five at this geography. The other themes are [Income & Poverty](../county-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../county-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../county-housing/collection.json) and [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../county-wellbeing/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../counties/collection.json), carries all 135 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. GEOIDs nest by prefix: `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` is the state, and tracts and block groups join back on their own first 5 characters. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [ZCTAs](../../zctas/catalog.json), [places and CDPs](../../places/catalog.json) and [congressional districts](../../congressional-districts/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet, minus the `*_moe` columns, and at every zoom the tiles are the real census geographies — there are few enough features here to draw them all at a national zoom, so this archive needs none of the coarser-geography coarse-zoom bands the catalog's finer collections carry. Built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo). Statistics still come from the GeoParquet: margins of error are not in the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

styles/default.title: No home internet
styles/default.description: Share of households with no internet subscription of any kind, pale to deep blue. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 6.5%/9%/11%/14%/18%, which fall at the 20th/40th/56th/76th/90th percentile of the national distribution. 4.1% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/no-vehicle.title: Households without a vehicle
styles/no-vehicle.description: Share of households with no vehicle available, pale yellow through teal to navy. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 3.5%/5%/6%/7.5%/10%, which fall at the 18th/42nd/59th/77th/90th percentile of the national distribution. 14.71% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/transit-commute.title: Commute by public transit
styles/transit-commute.description: Share of workers commuting by public transportation, pale yellow to dark green; the first class is deliberately narrow because most of the country has effectively none. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 0.5%/2%/5%/10%/25%, which fall at the 72nd/94th/98th/99th/100th percentile of the national distribution. 58.69% of counties have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 at this geography, too many to fade without washing the map out, so read pct_commute_transit_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single county.

styles/work-from-home.title: Work from home
styles/work-from-home.description: Share of workers whose usual commute is none — they worked from home — pale lilac to deep purple. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 5.5%/7.5%/9.5%/12%/17%, which fall at the 21st/39th/58th/75th/92nd percentile of the national distribution.

source-table-shells.description: `Table ID|Line|Indent|Unique ID|Label|Title|Universe|Type` for every table in the release. Two jobs here: every line number the build reads is pinned against this file and a vintage that renumbers a line fails the build, and every universe quoted in the column descriptions is this file's own `Universe` field. Served by census.gov.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — counties and county equivalents (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The geometry this collection joins onto, shoreline-clipped and generalized for mapping. Only the join key, the name parts and the land-area field are kept; reprojected from NAD83 to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. Served by census.gov.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 5-character county (or county-equivalent) GEOID — state (2) + county (3), e.g. `29510` for St. Louis city. Includes Puerto Rico municipios and the island-area county equivalents. Matches `GEOID` in the 2024 cartographic boundary county file; the ACS `0500000US` prefix is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: Human-readable name from the cartographic boundary county file: `NAMELSAD`, `STATE_NAME` — "St. Louis city, Missouri".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.40% of counties — the 13 island-area county equivalents (AS 5, GU 1, MP 4, VI 3), which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: hh_no_vehicle
table:columns.description: Occupied housing units with no vehicle available, owner- and renter-occupied combined. Universe: occupied housing units. Lines 3 + 10 of [B25044](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25044) (Tenure by Vehicles Available) — the "No vehicle available" line under each tenure — which is what makes this a tenure-blind count. Published as an integer; the two margins of error add in quadrature.

table:columns.name: hh_no_vehicle_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `hh_no_vehicle` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: pct_hh_no_vehicle
table:columns.description: Percent of occupied housing units with no vehicle available. Universe: occupied housing units. Lines 3 + 10 over line 1 of [B25044](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25044). Households, not people: a car-free household of four counts once.

table:columns.name: pct_hh_no_vehicle_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_hh_no_vehicle` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_hh_no_vehicle_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_hh_no_vehicle`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_drive_alone
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who drove alone to work in a car, truck or van. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Line 3 ("Drove alone", under "Car, truck, or van") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301) (Means of Transportation to Work). The ACS asks about the usual means of transportation in the reference week, so a hybrid commuter reports one mode.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_drive_alone_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_commute_drive_alone` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_transit
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who commuted by public transportation. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Line 10 ("Public transportation") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301), which covers bus, subway and elevated rail, light rail, commuter rail and ferryboat. Taxi and ride-hailing (line 16) are a separate category in this vintage and are **not** included.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_transit_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_commute_transit` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_walk_bike
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who walked or bicycled to work. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Lines 18 ("Bicycle") + 19 ("Walked") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301).

table:columns.name: pct_commute_walk_bike_moe

Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_work_from_home
table:columns.description: Percent of workers who worked from home. Universe: workers 16 years and over. Line 21 ("Worked from home") over line 1 of [B08301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08301). In a 2020–2024 5-year estimate this averages over the pandemic shift and its partial reversal, so it is not a reading of any single year.

table:columns.name: pct_work_from_home_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_work_from_home` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_commute_45min_plus
table:columns.description: Percent of commuters whose one-way travel time to work is 45 minutes or more. Universe: workers 16 years and over **who did not work from home** — the table's own universe, which is why work-from-home does not deflate this share. Lines 11 + 12 + 13 (45 to 59 minutes, 60 to 89, 90 or more) over line 1 of [B08303](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B08303) (Travel Time to Work).

table:columns.name: pct_commute_45min_plus_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_commute_45min_plus` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. table:columns.description: Percent of households with no internet access of any kind. Universe: households. Line 13 ("No Internet access") over line 1 of [B28002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B28002). Households that use the internet without paying for a subscription (line 12) are counted as having access, so this is the floor of the digital divide, not its full extent.

table:columns.name: pct_no_internet_moe

table:columns.name: pct_no_computer
table:columns.description: Percent of households with no computing device — no desktop or laptop, no smartphone, no tablet, no other computer. Universe: households. Line 11 ("No Computer") over line 1 of [B28001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B28001) (Types of Computers in Household).

table:columns.name: pct_no_computer_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_no_computer` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary county file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the county into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.
